stops.title: Group 16: Oxygen, anomalous behaviour, oxoacids & H₂SO₄
stops.inShort: Group 16 (O, S, Se, Te, Po): ns² np⁴. Oxygen shows anomalous behaviour (small size, high EN, no d-orbitals): diatomic gas O₂, −2 oxidation state, paramagnetic, H₂O is liquid due to H-bonding. Oxoacids of S: H₂SO₄, H₂S₂O₃ (thiosulphuric), H₂SO₅ (peroxymonosulphuric).

stops.title: Group 17: Halogens, interhalogen compounds & HCl/Cl₂
stops.inShort: Group 17 (F, Cl, Br, I, At): ns² np⁵. Thermal stability of hydrides: HF > HCl > HBr > HI. Acidic strength of oxoacids: HOCl < HClO₂ < HClO₃ < HClO₄. Bleaching powder: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O. Interhalogens: XX', XX'₃, XX'₅, XX'₇.

stops.title: Group 18: Noble gases & Xenon compounds
stops.inShort: Group 18 (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn): ns² np⁶ (except He 1s²). Neon is used in discharge tubes/advertising signs and beacon lights. Xenon forms fluorides (XeF₂, XeF₄, XeF₆) and oxides.

board.text: Write the balanced chemical equation, when excess of ammonia is treated with chlorine.
Write anomalous behaviour of oxygen with respect to: (i) Atomicity (ii) Oxidation state (iii) Magnetic property (iv) Nature of hydrides.
board.answer:
(i) Atomicity: Oxygen is diatomic (O₂), while S, Se, Te are polyatomic (S₈).
(ii) Oxidation state: Oxygen shows −2 (and −1, +2 in OF₂), whereas others show +2, +4, +6.
(iii) Magnetic property: O₂ is paramagnetic, others are diamagnetic.
(iv) Nature of hydrides: H₂O is a liquid at room temperature due to H-bonding; H₂S, H₂Se are gases.

board.text: What are interhalogen compounds? Write the chemical reaction, when chlorine reacts with dry slaked lime.
board.answer:
Interhalogen compounds are covalent compounds formed by the combination of two different halogens (general formula XX'_n, n = 1, 3, 5, 7, e.g. ClF₃, BrF₅).
Reaction with dry slaked lime: 2 Ca(OH)₂ + 2 Cl₂ → Ca(OCl)₂ + CaCl₂ + 2 H₂O (bleaching powder).

points.text: Balanced reaction of Cl₂ with dry Ca(OH)₂

board.text: Arrange the following in the increasing order of the property mentioned: (i) HOCl, HClO₂, HClO₃, HClO₄ (acidic strength) (ii) MF, MCl, MBr, MI (ionic character) (iii) HF, HCl, HBr, HI (thermal stability).
board.answer:
(i) Acidic strength: HOCl < HClO₂ < HClO₃ < HClO₄.
(ii) Ionic character: MI < MBr < MCl < MF.
(iii) Thermal stability: HI < HBr < HCl < HF.
